newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha campaigns to shore up support.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha campaigns to shore up support.

text.p: President Sali Berisha has hit Albania's rocky roads to appease of the mass of small savers ruined by get-rich-quick investment schemes.

The hard-pressed head of state travelled to this central industrial town on Wednesday to defend his administration's handling of the failure of several pyramid funds which has plunged Europe's poorest country into turmoil.

"I came to thank (the people) for the way they've dealt with their losses. We cannot pay their debts but we can intervene to speed up growth and the ensure economic recovery of the people," he said before entering the town's bleak sports hall where he adressed some 1,500 hand-picked supporters.

A month of riots and protests by investors who have lost their life savings when the schemes folded have posed the most serious challenge to Berisha's rule since he was elected in 1992 on a free-market ticket and promises of speedy growth.

Many of the savers and the country's opposition parties are blaming the government for not having stepped in to curb the growth of the funds and for failing to warn Albanians, new to the pitfalls of capitalism after decades of Stalinist isolation, of the risks.
Five high-risk schemes, in which an estimated $1 to $2 billion had been invested, collapsed in January.
In the capital Tirana, Vefa -- the country's biggest company with interests ranging from supermarkets to mining -- said it would start paying out all deposits by small investors immediately.

In a bid to calm investors' nerves and to disperse hundreds of people who have stood outside its offices for the past month, the group said it would start by giving full refunds to all investors who had put up to $5,000 in the company.
A Vefa spokesman said some 60 percent of its 80,000 investors would fall into that group. Investors having put in more than $5,000 would be reimbursed later.

In the southern town of Vlore,where clashes between protesters and police left three dead last week, some 3,000 marchers turned out for a candle-lit evening procession on the 15th successive day of street demonstrations.

Demonstrators demand the government's resignation and reimbursment of losses caused by the collapse of two local schemes. A group of 46 students, whose leaders were scheduled to meet a government delegation on Thursday, has threatened to stage a hunger strike to press home their demands.
Berisha told his party faithful in Elbasan that he would soon travel to Vlore.
Asked about his message to the people of Vlore, he told reporters: "They are very brave. They have had huge losses. I am very sad but I am sure I will find a common language with them."

Berisha's ruling Democratic Party has called a mid-day rally in Tirana. The opposition Social-Democrats were given permission for a rally in a stadium several km (miles) outside Tirana, but it was uncertain they would go ahed with the meeting which they originally wanted to hold in the capital.
